target_customer: Small satellite and CubeSat builders and operators needing propulsion
problem: Small satellites lacked low-cost, low-toxicity thrusters, since heritage hydrazine propulsion is toxic and expensive to handle.
business_model: Hardware sales of thrusters, multi-thruster modules and turnkey propulsion systems, plus custom design

founders.name: Erik Franks
previous_startups: Two earlier startups per his YC bio, not named
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he raised $2.3M, managed a 50-person team and won 20+ NASA contracts and competitions.

founders.name: Jeff Gibson
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page, no bio.

founders.name: Jake Teufert
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page, no bio.

exit.reason: Benchmark Space Systems took a permanent licensing partnership integrating Tesseract IP, assets and staff; no financial terms stated.

competitors.name: Busek
competitors.what: Ion, Hall and electrospray thrusters for small satellites
competitors.traction_then: BIT-3 ion thruster completed two critical design reviews for CubeSat missions

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing and flight-qualifying bipropellant thrusters is hardware engineering that needs testing facilities and reliability standards.

defensibility.rationale: Flight heritage and qualified hardware are slow to copy, but several funded thruster makers existed already.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; in August 2020 Benchmark Space Systems took a licensing partnership absorbing Tesseract's IP, assets and staff.

market_need_then: Growth in CubeSat and smallsat launches created demand for propulsion; a 2017 NASA slide deck notes many small-satellite propulsion technologies were still under development.

branding.domain_note: Uses tesseract.space; no source on how it was obtained.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, focused on green propulsion, cost and reliability per its site

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The word tesseract is shared with many other products, and the company was absorbed into Benchmark in 2020.

outcome_analysis: Tesseract built green bipropellant thrusters after YC Summer 2017 but no priced venture round was found in sources I could verify. In August 2020 Benchmark Space Systems integrated its intellectual property, assets and staff through a licensing partnership and Erik Franks joined Benchmark leadership. The reason is not stated, so the failure factor reflects only the absence of found later funding and is low confidence.
notes: Unverified single-source figures not recorded as rounds: Dealroom lists a $120K YC-led seed in 2017, and a Wefunder page shows about 919K from 1,226 investors (Wefunder page returned 403). The directory status is Active while a 2020 licensing deal absorbed the company; nanosats.eu lists it as inactive. A $13M Lockheed round in 2023 belonged to Agile Space Industries, not Tesseract. Competitor Accion source is a 2017 NASA slide deck comparison of CubeSat thrusters. Name origin search found nothing. Completeness pass: the 120K 2017 seed rests on Dealroom alone. The Wefunder crowdfunding campaign (SAFE) closed December 2018 per KingsCrowd, which shows 960K committed; the Wefunder page figure of about 919K and CrowdfundInsider's mid-campaign 346K conflict, so the amount is left null.
